about: The reference posters: Quartr's earnings-call posters on X (designers Oliver Hamrin, Haris Cehic, Jacob Titus). The kit downloads them for study from X's public image CDN, or cuts them from Oliver Hamrin's public portfolio videos; they are never stored in this skill. Notes on each are in references/swipe.md.

posters.idea: Jensen Huang's leather jacket hangs alone on a coat rack in a dark room: is he leaving or coming back?
posters.move: the founder's signature object, standing in for the founder, at a moment of succession talk
posters.medium: low-key monochrome photograph, film grain and dust

posters.idea: Nu's purple broken into pixels that drip down from the top and rise up from the bottom like a mirrored signal.
posters.move: the brand colour as the whole picture, digital bank as digital pixels
posters.medium: flat pixel mosaic in four tints of Nu purple (#820AD1) plus near-black, on paper

posters.idea: Cockroaches scattered across a red poster, one crawling over the copy.
posters.move: the unglamorous thing the business exists to fight, shot like fashion
posters.medium: photographic cut-outs on a flat signal-red field

posters.idea: A wall of '.com' set in twenty different typefaces.
posters.move: the one thing the company owns (the .com registry), repeated until it's a texture
posters.medium: typography as image, yellow on black inside a yellow frame

posters.idea: A tiny horse-drawn carriage on a field of loose red watercolour checks, from the house's equestrian roots.
posters.move: the company's heritage (it began as a harness maker), in a medium that fits the brand
posters.medium: watercolour and gouache; one of twelve variants the team posted

posters.idea: A silver Tesla flips through the dark trailing rocket smoke, the quarter staged like a launch.
posters.move: the product doing the founder's other business (SpaceX), a promise made literal
posters.medium: CGI/AI photograph on pure black, smoke lit cold white

posters.idea: A pixel-art mountain: a black rock under a red sky.
posters.move: the name made literal, in a childlike medium for a $15T asset manager
posters.medium: flat 8-bit pixel landscape, six colours, inside a white page

posters.idea: A line of identical blue 911s curving across a white page like a road or a chart line.
posters.move: the product repeated into a shape that means something (growth curve, racing line)
posters.medium: repeated product photograph on white

posters.idea: A tree whose leaves are green price tags ($1.25, $1.50, $3.00) and whose trunk is brown ones.
posters.move: the name made literal, out of the company's real material (its price tags)
posters.medium: photo collage of real price stickers on dark green

posters.idea: 'SOFTWARE THAT DOMINATES' typed over and over in monospace, with Palantir's ring logo ghosted out of the text.
posters.move: the company's own boast, turned into the texture that draws its logo
posters.medium: monospace typography as image, grey on white

posters.idea: 'Move fast and break things' bursts out from the centre like shattered glass over a pixel map.
posters.move: the founder's old motto, made to do what it says
posters.medium: radial typography over flat pixel shapes in Meta blue with one magenta accent

posters.idea: Sundar Pichai in halftone black and white, wearing a crown of Gemini sparkles.
posters.move: the CEO crowned by the product of the moment
posters.medium: halftone portrait plus a flat colour graphic element

posters.idea: A classical marble bust wearing Meta's infinity logo as a pair of VR goggles; the copy runs along the logo's loop.
posters.move: the logo turned into the product (glasses/headset), on the oldest kind of face
posters.medium: engraving-style bust on paper with one hand-drawn blue stroke

posters.idea: A torn-paper collage of excavators, bulldozers and quarries in Cat yellow, brown and black.
posters.move: the machines themselves, as a vintage industrial collage
posters.medium: collage of archival photos with yellow duotone patches

posters.idea: A fox Robin Hood drawing his bow, engraved in an oval frame on green bookcloth.
posters.move: the name made literal through a cultural reference (the fox Robin Hood)
posters.medium: antique engraving printed tone-on-tone on linen

posters.idea: A banana plant at night, one yellow bunch glowing among dark leaves.
posters.move: the product where it grows, shot like nature photography
posters.medium: flash-lit night photograph

posters.idea: A Figma canvas holding Quartr's own posters, with multiplayer cursors saying 'plz fix', 'crisp' and 'thanks bruv'.
posters.move: the product used as the medium (meta)
posters.medium: UI screenshot staged as a poster

posters.idea: Alex Karp's wild hair, his face lost in a white blur crossed by a band of half-legible text.
posters.move: the CEO's signature look, with the mystery Palantir sells
posters.medium: black-and-white portrait with a blur and a type band

posters.idea: Three burgers tumbling through the dark in slow motion, with one hard shadow on the floor.
posters.move: the cheapest product in the world, shot like a luxury campaign
posters.medium: food photograph on a dark brown gradient

posters.idea: The prancing horse as a real black horse, rearing in deep red shadow.
posters.move: the logo made literal
posters.medium: photograph in monochrome red light

posters.idea: A red apple whose inside is packed with circuit boards.
posters.move: the logo made literal, with the product inside
posters.medium: surreal still-life composite on pale grey

posters.idea: 'So like how long you been doing Uber?' over a motion-blurred back-seat view of city lights.
posters.move: the line every rider has said, as the headline
posters.medium: motion-blurred night photograph with a centred quote

making_of.what: Haris Cehic's 'How we made the NVIDIA poster': ~25 iterations with the team's verdicts written on them
